role: Independent read-only review by attention worker; no main checkout edits or extra builds
conclusions: SGD and AdamW scalar expression order and the weight-derived physical addressing of all operands match original ops.cpp 12181-12305. Checked extent validation covers those accesses, while conservative alias rejection avoids mutable alias-dependent semantics.

State replacement occurs only after all three outputs are built successfully. Graph moment projections depend on one AdamW node, and evaluate_many marks the dependency union before a single insertion-order evaluation. Repeated targets share one result; an error drops all unreturned snapshots.

Owned Send+Sync callbacks and higher-ranked task lifetimes cannot retain borrowed output state. Output bytes and initialization bits share one mutex; bounds are checked before slicing. Callback errors and unwind panics discard partial output.

The scoped launch gate defers callbacks until all requested workers are created. On launch failure started threads receive disabled and join; on callback failure all workers join before discarding output. Source n_tasks/task capping and empty-output suppression match frozen constructors/planner.

The independent fixtures compare 300 optimizer cases / 440704 output bytes and 260 custom cases / 30064 output bytes per profile, with full binary cursor exhaustion and expected counts. Tests additionally exercise graph output sharing, physical bounds, alias rejection, budget errors, callback ownership and mid-callback cancellation.
The domain documents accurately qualify missing mutable aliases, in-place custom behavior, complete training/scheduler integration and aggregate retained-memory budgets.
qualifications: Read-only source/provenance review, not an independent full test rerun. Parent owns integrated executions.
The supplied native optimizer captures cover single exceptional operands; arbitrary multi-NaN payload behavior is explicitly outside the equivalence guarantee.

The existing Tensor::from_bytes converts a Vec to Arc storage through the standard allocation path. Output byte limits do not bound that temporary peak, bitmap/thread-stack overhead, or every process allocation. The broad statement that all allocations are fallible should be read narrowly or qualified; this is a pre-existing tensor ownership boundary, not a newly introduced memory-safety defect.

The new optimizer failure test injects cancellation before a step, while code checks during loops and before publication. The custom test does inject cancellation after output writes. No concrete atomicity defect was found.
